Neskon.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
[[Trooper]]{{Fn|2}} '''Neskon''' was a [[Guardsman]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]].{{Fn|1a}}


==Biography==
An original [[Tanith]] member of the [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]], Neskon was one of the Tanith First's dedicated [[Imperial Flamer|flame]]-[[Special Weapons Trooper|troopers]].{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|3}}

In the closing stages of the [[Siege of Vervunhive]], Neskon was one of thirty Tanith selected personally by [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt]] to take part in [[Operation Heironymo]], the mission to infiltrate [[The Spike]] and assassinate [[Heritor Asphodel]].{{Fn|1b}} While storming the bridge of the Spike, the Imperials faced Asphodel's elite bodyguard cadre, the [[Darkwatch]], with Neskon losing his left leg to a Darkwatcher armed with a [[pike-axe]].{{Fn|1c}}

Neskon, however, recovered from his injuries and went on to participate in the regiment's actions on [[Hagia]]{{Fn|2}} and [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]].{{Fn|3}}

Nessa Bourah.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Nessa Bourah'''{{Fn|3f}} was a [[Verghast]]ite [[Imperial Guard Sniper|Sniper]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]].{{Fn|3a}}


==Biography==
===Verghast===
Nessa was born in [[Vervunhive]] on the planet [[Verghast]] in '''341.748.[[M41]]'''.{{Fn|3f}} A teenager by the time of the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade|Sabbat Crusade's]] actions on Verghast{{Fn|1a}}, she was a nurse-in-training when the [[Chaos|fallen]] [[Ferrozoica|Hive Ferrozoica]] [[Siege of Vervunhive|attacked]] Vervunhive.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}} Stationed in the outer habs, she managed to survive the Zoicans' initial artillery bombardment of the hive and, along with a number of other civilians, met up with a unit of the [[Vervun Primary]] led by [[Captain (Imperial Guard)|Captain]] [[Olin Fencer]].{{Fn|1a}}

Fencer [[Conscript|recruited]] all of the able-bodied civilians he found to reinforce his [[Imperial Guard Company|company's]] defensive position, knowing that the Zoicans would lead an infantry advance. Nessa was placed in charge of a field hospital stocked with medical supplies from a bombed-out mine. When the Zoicans ceased the artillery fire and led their first infantry assault on Vervunhive, Fencer's company's position was overrun and Fencer himself was killed.{{Fn|1a}} The survivors, including Nessa, regrouped as a [[Scratch Company]] led by the miner [[Gol Kolea]].{{Fn|1b}}

In the final stages of the Siege of Vervunhive, Kolea's scratch company was detailed by [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt]] to guide a force of [[Imperial Guardsmen]] through the hive to [[Operation Heironymo|attack the enemy command vehicle]] and assassinate [[Asphodel|their leader]].{{Fn|1c}}

At the conclusion of the war on Verghast, Vervunhive was reduced to ruins and planned to be demolished. [[Warmaster]] [[Macaroth]] issued an [[Act of Consolation]], allowing any surviving Vervunhiver to sign up for the [[Astra Militarum]] and reinforce one of the Sabbat Crusade's [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiments]] that had been sent to aid the hive.{{Fn|1d}} Kolea's scratch company all took the offer and were recruited into the [[Tanith First and Only]], the legendary ''"[[Ibram Gaunt|Gaunt's]] Ghosts"''.{{Fn|1d}}{{Fn|2a}}

===Sabbat Worlds Crusade===
As a [[Trooper]] in the Tanith First, Nessa had to overcome a number of obstacles - she was a Verghastite (and therefore a newcomer, seen by some of the Tanith as unworthy of being Ghosts) and a woman (prior to the Act of Consolation, the Tanith had been an all-male regiment).{{Fn|2a}} In addition she, like many of the other Verghastite recruits, was deaf due to exposure to the Zoican artillery bombardment and so had to make use of lip-reading and improvised sign language.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|2a}} Despite this, Nessa was regarded as an excellent shot{{Fn|1c}}{{Fn|2a}}, with [[Captain (Imperial Guard)|Captain]] [[Ban Daur|Daur]] believing that she and a number of the other women of Verghast would one day challenge the Tanith's established expert [[Imperial Guard Sniper|snipers]] like [[Hlaine Larkin|Larkin]] and [[Rilke]].{{Fn|2a}} She even managed to be one of the first Verghastites to be allowed to train for the regiment's marksmen corps.{{Fn|2c}}

On [[Hagia]], the first theatre of the Sabbat Crusade that the regiment fought on after Verghast, the Tanith First were part of the assault on the [[Holy Doctrinopolis]]. Nessa was wounded by an [[Infardi]] [[Chaos Cultist|cultist]] that shot her in the gut.{{Fn|2a}} She was left behind in the Doctrinopolis with the rest of the injured Tanith when [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt|Gaunt]] was later ordered by [[Lord General]] [[Lugo]] to escort an honour guard to the [[Shrinehold of Saint Sabbat]] and retrieve [[Saint Sabbat|the Saint's]] remains in preparation for the evacuation of Hagia. However Nessa's officer, [[Colonel]] [[Colm Corbec|Corbec]], who was also among the wounded left in the city, had been experiencing visions of the Saint beckoning him to the Shrinehold. When Corbec decided to take a [[Chimera]] and follow the visions, Nessa was one of five Troopers who accompanied him on the journey.{{Fn|2b}}

By the time of the regiment's deployment on [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]], Nessa had completed her specialised training and been officially inducted as a [[Imperial Guard Sniper|sniper]].{{Fn|3a}} She was attached to Kolea's [[Imperial Guard Platoon|platoon]] prior to the assault on [[Cirenholm]].{{Fn|3b}}

Later in the campaign she was selected personally by Gaunt as part of the Tanith component of [[Operation Larisel]].{{Fn|3c}} Nessa, along with [[Doyl]], [[Brin Milo|Milo]] and the [[Phantine Skyborne|Skyborne Specialist]] [[Lex Cardinale|Cardinale]], were assigned to team Larisel 3 under [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Adare]].{{Fn|3d}}{{Fn|3e}}

==Trivia==
{{Trivia}}
Nessa is the only one of the Tanith First to be consistently referred to by her first name as opposed to her surname.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Lieutenant (Space Marine)|Lieutenant-Commander]] of the [[World Eaters]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] active during the [[Horus Heresy]].

===Overview===
Nigh Vash Delerax took part in the [[Dropsite Massacre]]. However much to his displeasure, he was prevented by the [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] from taking part in the battle on [[Isstvan V]] and instead commanded the [[Battle Barge]] ''[[Dedicated Wrath]]'', during the void battle against the Loyalist's ships. After the Massacre was completed, Delerax was assigned to track down and destroy any Loyalist ships in the [[Isstvan System]], that had survived the battle. Though he took delight in destroying any surviving loyalists' ships he encountered, Delerax was angered at having an [[Alpha Legion]] member aboard the Dedicated Wrath, who served as Horus' ambassador to ensure the Warmaster's orders were being followed. The only thing that kept Delerax's anger in check, was that his second-in-command, [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Althix Kordassis]], acted as a go between and minder for the Alpha Legion member, who claimed he was the [[Primarch]] [[Alpharius]]. His mood brighten greatly however, after he received a message that his Primarch [[Angron]] was hunting down [[Corax]] and the remnants of the [[Raven Guard]] on Isstvan V.{{Fn|1}}

After destroying a stricken [[Salamanders]] [[Strike Cruiser]], Delerax immediately gave the order to race towards Isstvan V; as he was intent to take part in the direct combat that was earlier denied to him. Once they neared the world though, Delerax received a message stating the Warmaster wanted the Dedicated Wrath to join with the Traitor Legion ships in the area and destroy a [[Therion Cohort|Loyalist fleet]] that was discovered near [[Isstvan IV]]. Delerax refused the order at first, but when Horus' ambassador Alpharius contacted him and demanded the Lieutenant-Commander do as he was ordered, Delerax relented. However when the Dedicated Wrath suddenly detected another fleet above Isstvan V, Delerax realized they were intent on evacuating the surviving Raven Guard and ordered an immediate attack on this [[Branne Nev|new Loyalist fleet]].{{Fn|1}}

When Alpharius discovered that Delerax had disobeyed his orders once again, the Alpha Legion member contacted Delerax in order to enforce the Warmaster's rule. The Lieutenant-Commander would not be dissuaded this time though, as his Battle Barge was the only ship in the area that could stop the Loyalists from achieving their goal. This led Alpharius to confront Delerax on the Dedicated Wrath's bridge, just as it was preparing to fire upon the Loyalists. In the heated discussion that followed, Alpharius claimed that it was decided that Corax and the remnants of his Legion would be allowed to escape, as they still had a [[Battle of Ravendelve|part to play]] in the Imperium's civil war. Delerax refused to believe Alpharius and ordered the Alpha Legion member to remove himself from the bridge or be killed.{{Fn|2}}

It was at that moment though, that Captain Kordassis placed a [[bolt pistol]] to Delerax's head. Incensed at this betrayal, the Lieutenant-Commander asked what Kordassis was doing and it was revealed that a member of the Alpha Legion, was wearing his now dead second-in-command's face. An enraged Delerax then attempted to grab the bolt pistol, but Kordassis' doppelganger pulled the trigger and killed the Lieutenant-Commander{{Fn|1}}. However after his death, another member of the Alpha Legion took Delerax's face and masqueraded as the Lieutenant-Commander for a number of years, until the [[Battle of Yarant]]. It was during that battle with the Raven Guard and [[Space Wolves]], that Delerax's doppelganger met his end in an assassination strike by a [[Dark Fury]] squadron, led by [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Ghelt]].{{Fn|2}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was an [[Admiral]] in the '''[[Jupiter|Jovian]] Void Clan Fleets''' and [[Imperial Army]], who took part in the [[Great Crusade]] and the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}}

===History===
Due to her skills in void warcraft, she was chosen by the [[Primarch]] [[Rogal Dorn]] to serve in his '''Solar Command Staff''', as he prepared to defend [[Terra]] from [[Horus]]' treachery{{Fn|1a}}. As Niora aided the Primarch though, she was left to wonder about the fate of her daughter, [[Khalia Su-Kassen Hon II]], who was [[Imperial Navy Captain|Captain]] of the Imperial Army warship ''[[Thunder Break]]''. It had been attached to the [[Sons of Horus]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]'s [[Sixty-Third Expeditionary Fleet]], during the [[Great Crusade]] and nothing had been heard of the warship since the Heresy began. However after the [[White Scars]] Legion later returned to [[Terra]], Niora developed a friendship of sorts with its Primarch [[Jaghatai Khan]] who, after learning of her daughter{{Fn|1b}}, used his influence to have resources diverted to discover Khalia's fate. It was as the [[Solar War]] raged, that the Thunder Break's destruction at the traitors' hands, after Khalia refused to join in Horus' betrayal, was found written on a report detailing the numerous wrecks found in the [[Isstvan System]]. Once he learned of this, [[Malcador the Sigilite]] personally informed Niora of her daughter's death.{{Fn|1c}}

The Admiral would have little time to grieve, as Horus' forces neared Terra's moon, [[Luna]], and in response the Primarch Dorn transferred himself, Niora and half of the Solar Command Staff to the [[Phalanx]] [[fortress-monastery]]. This was to better coordinate, the Imperium's forces as the Chaos fleet approached Terra, but the Solar Command was unaware that the worse was still to come{{Fn|1d}}. As the Solar War had begun, a massive Chaos ritual had been enacted, that would allow Horus and his main fleet to transport near Terra from the Warp and it was finished as the Solar Command Staff landed upon the Phalanx. The completed ritual caused a large amount of etheric energy to be unleashed and the [[Daemon]] [[Samus]] then used it, to possess the [[Remembrancer]] [[Mersadie Oliton]] and through her, the Daemon opened a Warp breech aboard the Phalanx{{Fn|1e}}. This allowed a horde of Daemons to appear aboard the fortress and Niora took part in defending the Phalanx, long enough for Mersadie to temporarily free herself from Samus. Before the Daemon could regain control of her, the Remembrancer committed suicide which closed the Warp breach and caused the Daemons to disappear{{Fn|1f}}. In the aftermath of the attack, Dorn stated he would go to Terra and defend it, as Horus' forces had reached [[Mankind]]'s Homeworld. Before he left though, the Primarch transferred control of the Phalanx to Niora and she took overall command of the Imperium's surviving warships in the Sol System, as the [[Siege of Terra]] began.{{Fn|1g}}

Still in command of the ''Phalanx'' and operating in the void at the edge of the Sol System, Su-Kassen was shocked to find that [[Dark Angels]] under [[Corswain]] had arrived to aid the loyalists in the Siege.{{Fn|2}} She later provided the ''[[Imperator Somnium]]'' to Corswain's forces in order to have the Dark Angels break the traitor blockade and land on Terra.{{Fn|3}}

In the final stages of the Siege of Terra, Su-Kassen and [[Halbract]] observed the reactivation of the [[Astronomican]] and took it as a sign that the time was now for their counterattack. They launched the ''Phalanx'' and their surviving warships at the traitors just hours before the arrival of [[Guilliman]]'s reinforcements fleet.{{Fn|4}}

Nirriam.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Nirriam''' was a [[Verghast]]ite{{Fn|1c}} [[Guardsman]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]].{{Fn|1a}}


==Biography==
During the assault on [[Cirenholm]] on the planet [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]], Nirriam was among those Tanith Guardsmen onboard [[drop-ship]] '''2K''' under the command of [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeants]] [[Haller]] and [[Dohon Domor|Domor]]. However, on approach to the city, 2K was damaged by [[Blood Pact|the enemy's]] air defences and crashlanded on the outside of Cirenholm's secondary dome.{{Fn|1a}}

The survivors of the crash made their way inside the dome via an air vent and eventually made their way to the control chamber of the dome's vapour mill.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1c}} On reaching the control chamber, Nirriam was tasked with operating its [[vox]] array in the hopes of contacting the regiment's [[Ibram Gaunt|commanding officer]]. Although Nirriam was classed as a standard infantryman and had only rudimentary vox training{{Fn|1c}}, he was still the best man for the job, as both of the [[vox-officer]]s who were aboard 2K ([[Gohho]] and [[Liglis]]) died in the crash.{{Fn|1b}}

Nmembo.wikitext:
{{AdeptusCustodesPortal}}
'''Nmembo''' was a [[Hetaeron Compaion]] in the [[Legio Custodes]], who took part in the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
A proven exemplar of the [[Legio Custodes|Custodes]]' excellence,{{Fn|2}} he was among the one hundred [[Hetaeron Companions]]{{Fn|1e}} that [[Caecaltus Dusk]] commanded as the [[Emperor]] led a [[Teleportation]] attack on [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]]' flagship, the [[Vengeful Spirit]]. But due to Horus' machinations, the strike force's teleportation separated them all and the Emperor and the Companions found themselves alone within one of the Spirit's hanger bays.{{Fn|1b}} Soon afterwards, though, the Warmaster is able to manipulate the Companions' minds and convinces them that the Emperor must die. With this overwhelming thought, the Companions attack the Emperor and He is forced to kill many of them, before He can gather enough of His [[psychic]] might to clear the Custodes' minds of Horus' influence.{{Fn|1c}} The Companions have been ravaged, however, and few are still alive to protect the Emperor, as He ventures further into the Vengeful Spirit.{{Fn|1d}}

Their respite is short lived though, as the [[Chaos Gods]] strike and cloud the [[Hetaeron Companions|Companions]]' minds to the environment around them. This allows the [[Daemons]] infesting the [[warp]]-tainted [[Vengeful Spirit]] to silently attack the [[Legio Custodes|Custodes]] and many are killed this way, before the [[Emperor]] notices what is happening. Once more He is forced to use his [[psychic]] powers to clear the Companions' minds, but at this point only Nmembo, [[Caecaltus Dusk]], [[Xadophus]], [[Karedo]], [[Taurid]], [[Ravengast]] and [[Zagrus]] still live.{{Fn|1e}} As they venture further into the Vengueful Spirit they begin to be attacked on all sides and the Emperor extends his psychic might into the surviving Companions. Though their minds are still their own, the Custodes' become an extension of the Emperor's will and their eight bodies are controlled by His mind, as He searches for [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]].{{Fn|2}}

'''Nokad the Blighted''' (also known as '''Nokad the Smiling''') was a [[Chaos]] [[Magister]]{{Cite this}} in the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade]] in [[M41]]. He was well over two metres tall, and wore various loops rings, chains, and spikes on his body.{{Fn|1}}

One of Nokad's first acts was to use his forces to conquer the planet [[Bucephalon]] from within. He then had all the leaders of Bucephalon's capital city-state's thirty-two [[Noble House|noble families]] crucified to walls, and hung their own heraldic banners there with them. Bucephalon's loss was a great tragedy, as it was considered one of the most honourable of the [[Sabbat Worlds]], and was listed by [[Warmaster]] [[Slaydo]] in his great liberation address at the start of the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade]] as one of the worlds he was most eager to save.{{Fn|1}}

Nokad eventually met his death at the hands of the sniper [[Hlaine Larkin]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Regiment]], who shot him through the head as he was singing devotional hymns to his troops. With the Magister dead, the Chaos forces' morale crumbled, and the planet was reconquered by the [[Imperium]].{{Fn|1}}

'''Nomus Rhy'tan''' was a [[Lord Chaplain]] of the [[Salamanders]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

===Overview===
When Chaplains came to the Salamanders Legion, it fell upon fertile ground as the spiritual discipline of the Legion and the philosophy of the [[Great Crusade]] were already considered greatly important to the Salamanders. The direct promulgation of the doctrines of [[Vulkan]], shaped by the culture of [[Nocturne]], were already being distributed by the 'Voices of Fire' - a body of chosen Legionaries of which Nomus Rhy'tan was already among.{{Fn|1}}

Many of these men went on to become the Legion's first great generation of Chaplains and Rhy'tan already was highly regarded as a confidant of Vulkan as well as a renowned orator. Rhy'tan was left behind by Vulkan before the [[Drop Site Massacre]] with the duty of overseeing the Legion's [[Neophyte]]s and acting as Regent in his stead. Thus he survived the massacre of his Legion, and was the one who had to pick up its fragmented pieces after Vulkan went missing.{{Fn|1}}

Nomus Rhy'tan proved a key loyalist commander when [[Death Guard]] forces later [[Battle of Nocturne|assaulted Nocturne]].{{Fn|2}}

'''Nork Deddog''' is an [[Ogryn]] in the [[Imperial Guard]] possessing enhanced brain power and strength coupled with the loyalty of a [[Commissar]]. 

===Biography===
By Ogryn standards, Nork is a genius, given that he can write his name (or at least the first initial of it), count as high as four and even speak in short sentences.  These are rare (if not unique) achievements in Ogryn development. For this reason, he was taken out of the normal stream of warfare and underwent artificial mental enhancement (possibly the same process used in the creation of [[Bone 'ead]]s) and was soon training within a special unit{{Fn|1}}.

He was then assigned to the [[Catachan 2nd Jungle Fighters Regiment|2nd Catachan]] under [[Colonel]] [[Greiss]], fighting on [[Balur]]. He was quickly taken as the Colonel's bodyguard, and the sight of the two together became more frequent for the four years the wars lasted. Often they were seen together on the battlefield with Greiss bawling orders and explosive shells bouncing off Nork's dense skull. It is known he has saved the Colonel's life on many occasions, including carrying his wounded body from a disaster at [[Breakback Hill]]. When Colonel Greiss was injured during the action, he ordered Nork to retrieve the medi-kit from his [[Chimera]], which had taken damage and was perched up-ended in a drainage ditch.  Nork proceeded to drag the Chimera out of the ditch and twenty yards down the road to the injured Colonel because, as he put it, ''"Da medi-kit is in da carrier, surr."''{{Fn|2}}

His reputation for loyalty is unsurpassed and his skills as a bodyguard are in high demand by [[Imperium]] officers across the sector. When [[Ork]] [[Warboss]] [[Uglurk Gitsmasha]] and his hardest mob of [[Meganobz]] charged an [[Imperial Guard]] command dugout, Nork Deddog was the only one to stand his ground beside Sub-overlord Ven Vambold. Nork killed the massive Ork Warlord with a single, extremely violent headbutt that left the remaining Orks totally awestruck and they retreated rather than face the angry Ogryn bodyguard.{{Fn|2}} Similarly, Nork fulfilled his role when Brigadier [[Aloysius van Burenvan]] was swallowed by a [[Tyranid]] [[Mawloc]] because of his own cowardice.{{Fn|4}}

Nork has saved the lives of hundreds, if not thousands of officers (and troopers) in battle, earning him a vast range of medals and notability among Imperial Officers.  He does not fight for these medals, however, but instead, using both his immense brawn and intelligence, he fights for the satisfaction of his superiors and the [[Imperium]].{{Fn|1}}

Nour.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
{{spoiler|source=The Guns of Tanith (Novel)}}
'''Nour''' was a [[Verghast]]ite{{Fn|1b}} [[Guardsman]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]].{{Fn|1a}} He fought as part of [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Gol Kolea|Kolea's]] [[Imperial Guard Platoon|platoon]].{{Fn|1d}}


==Biography==
When the Tanith First fought in the retaking of [[Cirenholm]] on the planet [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]], Nour sustained a burn from a [[las weapon]]. He attempted to conceal his injury after the battle in the hopes of keeping it as an honour scar, but [[Chief Medic]] [[Tolin Dorden|Dorden]] spotted the burn and was able to treat it before it became septic.{{Fn|1b}}

Nour was later one of sixteen Tanith First Guardsmen selected personally by the regiment's commander, [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt]], to take part in [[Operation Larisel]], the mission to infiltrate the city of [[Ouranberg]] and assassinate [[Sagittar Slaith|the leader]] of the [[Blood Pact]] force that had conquered Phantine.{{Fn|1c}} He was assigned to team Larisel 4 under [[Imperial Guard Scout|Scout]]-[[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Oan Mkoll|Mkoll]] alongside [[Cocoer]], [[Rilke]] and the [[Phantine Skyborne|Skyborne Specialist]] [[Arye Babbist|Babbist]].{{Fn|1e}}

Unfortunately, during the approach to [[Ouranberg]], Larisel 4's [[Marauder Bomber|Marauder]] was shot down by the city's air defences with all hands lost{{Fn|1e}}{{Fn|1f}} (save Mkoll, who managed to save himself with his [[grav-chute]]).{{Fn|1g}}

("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation =Member of the [[Raven Guard]]'s 66th Company{{Fn|5}} |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' *[[Corax]]'s [[Lycaeus]] rebels (Former) *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Raven Guard]] |Notes = }} '''Nykona Sharrowkyn''' was a member of the [[Raven Guard]] Legion's 66th Company{{Fn|5}} during the [[Horus Heresy]]. He was trained in "wraith-slipping" and could literally evade light and walk instinctively in shadows, giving him an almost ghost like ability to infiltrate {{Fn|2b}}. He held the incredible accolades of being one of few beings to shoot a [[Primarch]] in the head with a [[Sniper Rifle]]{{Fn|2a}} and survive, and also besting [[Lucius the Eternal]] twice in sword combat.{{Fn|2d}}{{Fn|2e}} ===History=== Nykona Sharrowkyn was born upon the enslaved moon of [[ Lycaeus]], growing up in the darkness of its prison blocs. In his youth he was assigned as a "salt boy", being forced to move down through Lucaeus' narrow and dangerous tunnels to gather salt from the moons tidal pools. Due to constantly changing tides and cave-ins, the duty was wrought with dangerous and mortality rates were high. Nonetheless, Nykona survived and at the age of thirteen was sent to the surface of the moon to be used for mining. He subsequently joined [[Corvus Corax]]'s rebellion against the slavers of [[Kiavahr]].{{Fn|3a}} Nykona later joined the [[Raven Guard]] as a [[Space Marine]] and took part in the [[Great Crusade]]. He was at [[Istvaan V]] with the rest of his Legion and during the [[Drop Site Massacre]] was wounded by traitors' bolter fire. After being seriously wounded he was rescued by fellow loyalist legionnaire [[Sabik Wayland]] from the [[Iron Hands]] Legion. Sharrowkyn and Wayland escaped the massacre aboard one of the Iron Hands' [[Storm Eagle]]s and joined the decimated remains of the Iron Hands.{{Fn|2a}} At some point during the Heresy, Sharrowkyn, accompanied by Wayland, was deployed to the [[Forge World]] of [[Cavor Sarta]] to recover the [[Kryptos]] machine. During this mission he killed one of the [[Word Bearers]] who was trying to save and hide one of the Kryptos.{{Fn|1}}: With the [[Kryptos]], Loyalist commanders were able to finally access the Traitors’ coded communications and allowing them to see their arranged meetings. Sharrowkyn remained with the Iron Hands ship [[Sisypheum]] and was inserted on to [[Hydra Cordatus]], to intercept the meeting of the traitor [[Primarch]]s [[Fulgrim]] and [[Perturabo]]. After learning of Fulgrim's intentions to enter the [[Eye of Terror]] and recover the Angel Exterminatus, he and his partner Sabik Wayland acted as a sniper pair and managed to shoot Fulgrim in the head. The Primarch did not die however, and was healed by [[Fabius Bile]]. Escaping two Legions and returning to the ''Sisypheum'', the decision is made to intercede in the traitors plan to acquire the unknown xenos weapon, taking them to the dead [[eldar]] world of [[Iydris]].{{Fn|2a}} After a disastrous experiment on the ships [[Plasma Reactor]]s by [[Frater Thamatica]]{{Fn|2c}}, the ''Sisypheum'' was boarded by both the [[Emperors Children]] and [[Iron Warriors]]. This was the first time Sharrowkyn crossed swords with [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]] and bested him in combat, cutting Lucius's face. He was unable to deliver a killing blow as the battle carried them away from each other.{{Fn|2d}} A reckoning then took place on the planet itself, when Nykona sought out Lucius and isolated him before swooping down to attack. Sharrowkyn bested him and plunged both of his gladii through his neck and chest, piercing both hearts, killing him and leaving his cadaver on the planet.{{Fn|2e}} [[Fabius Bile]] recovered Lucius's body and he somehow awoke in the Apothecarion - the method of his return to life is not clear.{{Fn|2f}} Nykona, still part of the ''Sisypheum's'' crew, later was part of the strike force that encountered the impostor [[Shadrak Meduson]], who was apparently [[Alpharius]] in disguise. During the battle, Sharrowkyn slew the skilled [[Alpha Legion]] combatant [[Ashur Maesan]] and saved the life of [[Cadmus Tyro]].{{Fn|3}} Nykona and the ''Sisypheum'' eventually managed to reach the [[Sol System]] by the time of the [[Siege of Terra]]. They received a distress signal from [[Ta'lab Vita-37]] and were drawn into a mission on [[Luna]] to rescue the [[Magna Mater]] from traitor clutches.{{Fn|4a}} During the mission all of the ''Sisypheum's'' crew save Sharrowkyn and Sabik Wayland were slain.{{Fn|4b}} A badly injured Wayland dropped Sharrowkyn off at an abandoned coaling station deep in the void before using the ''Sisypheum'' to draw away pursuing traitor vessels. Safeguarding the Magna Mater and with only the [[Psyber Eagle]] [[Garuda]] for company, Sharrowkyn put himself into a state of hibernation.{{Fn|4c}} ===Notes=== While Nykona is never specifically stated to be a member of the [[Mor Deythan]], his ability to utilize the wraith-walk through shadows would suggest he was amongst their members.{{Fn|2b}} ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Kryptos (Short Story)]] *2: [[Angel Exterminatus]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: Book 2, Chapter 5 **{{Endn|2b}}: Book 2, Chapter 10 **{{Endn|2c}}: Book 2, Chapter 12 **{{Endn|2d}}: Book 2, Chapter 14 **{{Endn|2e}}: Book 2, Chapter 26 **{{Endn|2f}}: Book 2, Chapter 27 *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Seventh Serpent (Novella)]] **{{Endn|3a}}: Chapter 6 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Sons of Selenar (Novella)]]: **{{Endn|4a}}: Chapter 3 **{{Endn|4b}}: Chapters 9-10 **{{Endn|4c}}: Chapter 11 **{{Endn|4d}}: Cover *{{Endn|5}}: [[The Horus Heresy: Legions]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Sharrowkyn, Nykona}} [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Raven Guard)]]

("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *Commander of the [[Iron Warriors]] [[114th Grand Battalion]] *Member of the [[Disciples of the Flames]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Iron Warriors]] (Former) **[[Disciples of the Flames]] |Notes = }} '''{{PAGENAME}}'''{{Fn|1}} (also spelled ''Narik Dreygur''{{Fn|3}}), known as the "Gravewalker" was a commander of the [[Iron Warriors]] during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}} ===Biography=== Once a respected Commander on [[Istvaan V]] he fell due to a [[Raven Guard]] [[Moritat]] having incinerated his flesh. This cost him favour with his [[Primarch]]. The [[Apolakron]] then rebuilt his broken body with many [[bionic]] implants and grafted a [[Cortex Controller]] to his nervous system. Joining their ranks he was now called "Gravewalker" and commanded [[Battle Automata]], becoming a [[Consul Praevian]].{{Fn|1}} During the [[Siege of Epsilon-Stranivar IX]], the immense losses endured by the [[114th Grand Battalion]] of the Iron Warriors due to abandonment by their [[Alpha Legion]] allies saw Dreygur as the most senior remaining commander. He later took part in the [[Siege of Mezoa]], again at the side of the Alpha Legion which used his forces as cannon fodder and bait. Disgusted by the Alpha Legion and moved by the words of honour of [[Cassian Dracos]], Dreygur switched sides and attacked [[Autilon Skorr]]'s Alpha Legion contingent. Afterward, Dreygur became a trusted confidant of Dracos.{{Fn|1}} ===Images=== [[Image:NarikMini.jpg|thumb|center|200px|Nârik Dreygur Miniature{{Fn|2}}]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Six - Retribution]] pgs. 38–44 & 253 *{{Endn|2}}: [https://www.forgeworld.co.uk/resources/fw_site/fw_pdfs/Horus_Heresy/Narik.pdf Forgeworld: Nârik Dreygur] (last accessed 14/04/2019) *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Horus Heresy: Legions]]: "Narik Dreygur" card {{DEFAULTSORT:Dreygur, Nârik}} [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Iron Warriors)]] [[Category:Loyalists from Traitor Legions]] [[de:Nârik Dreygur]] [[fr:Narik Dreygur]]

'''O'Vesh''', also known as '''Cloudspear''', is a [[T'au Empire]] [[T'au Commander|Commander]] from the [[Vior'la]] [[Sept]], who pilots an [[Enforcer Battlesuit]].{{Fn|1b}} She is currently in command of the [[Sudden Dawn Cadre|Sudden Dawn]] [[Hunter Cadre]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
Embodying all that it means to be a [[Vior'la]]n, O'Vesh is known to be bold and aggressive. She also has a flair for [[Mont'ka]] raids, that are high-risk, high-reward operations and will invariably lead her warriors from the front, while doing so.{{Fn|1b}} The [[T'au Commander]] believes strength in defense is no excuse for inactivity and those Commanders who wait for foes to come to them, are abdicating responsibility for a battle's flow. Doing so, she holds, hands the initiative to the [[T'au Empire]]'s enemies much like a [[Drone]] would relinquish a data-missive. To O'Vesh, such passivity is not the way of Vior'la.{{Fn|2}}

Oan Mkoll.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
[[Image:MkollMini9th.jpg|thumb|right|220px|''''Oan Mkoll''' Miniature{{Fn|15}}]]
'''Oan Mkoll''' was a [[Imperial Guard Scout|Scout]]-[[Imperial Guard Sergeant|Sergeant]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]] from their inception, serving in the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}} In an entire regiment noted for their stealth insertion abilities, Sergeant Mkoll stood out as the exemplar of stealth, tracking and scouting skills.{{Fn|2a}}


==Biography==
===Early Life===
{{Spoiler|source=Gaunt's Ghosts (Novel Series)}}
Before the Founding of the Guard regiments, Mkoll was a woodsman in the [[nalwood]] forests of [[Tanith]]. His wife [[Eiloni]] predeceased him (and Tanith itself) by several years, and both of his sons perished in the destruction of the planet.{{Fn|1i}}

===Astra Militarum===
Promoted to the rank of [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] and leader of the regiment's [[Imperial Guard Scout|scout unit]], Mkoll was widely respected for his superlative stealth and tracking skills and noted to be one of the finest scouts in the regiment by [[Colonel]] [[Colm Corbec]].{{Fn|1a}} On the forest planet of [[Ramillies 268-43]], Mkoll pursued traces of enemy activity deep into the wilderness and located a blind [[Chaos Dreadnought]], which he killed single-handed through a combination of his natural stealth skills, bravery, and realizing the uniquely hostile nature of the native flora which allowed him to distract the leviathan.{{Fn|2a}}

On [[Fortis Binary]], Colonel Corbec deployed Mkoll in the vanguard of his section during the Tanith 1st's counter-attack that would end up securing victory on the world. Mkoll's acute observational skills meant that he was the only one to notice that Trooper [[Skulane]]'s death had been caused by a corrupted Trooper [[Drayl]]; in warning the rest of the column he was lightly wounded.{{Fn|1b}} After the situation had been resolved and Corbec's unit linked up with that led by [[Ibram Gaunt]], Mkoll was once again deployed in the vanguard, this time of the larger force.{{Fn|1c}}

In the aftermath of some regimental downtime on the world of [[Pyrites]],{{Fn|1b}} Mkoll became involved in both the feud with the [[Jantine Patricians regiment]] and the machinations of the radical [[Inquisitor]], [[Heldane]], when he was assigned to the revenge team sent to cause havoc amongst the Jantine and rescue the kidnapped [[Major]] [[Elim Rawne|Rawne]].{{Fn|1d}}{{Fn|1e}}{{Fn|1f}}

On the regiment's next posting, the [[death world]] [[Menazoid Epsilon]], Mkoll led the entire scout [[platoon]] in advance, mapping out the land for those following. He diverted from the high command's assault path on Gaunt's orders, instead searching for an entranceway to an underground complex which would be revealed to contain a corrupted [[Standard Template Constructor]].{{Fn|1g}} Once Mkoll had located the complex, Gaunt assigned him to the commando team which ultimately destroyed the [[STC]].{{Fn|1h}}{{Fn|1i}}{{Fn|1j}}{{Fn|1k}}{{Fn|1l}}

On [[Monthax]], Mkoll performed the advanced scouting of the [[Chaos]] positions and also stumbled onto a ruined structure that he deduced was important to the enemy in some way. More strangely, Mkoll confessed that, having found the ruin once, he retraced his steps but was unable to find it again. Mkoll's own men thought their Sergeant may have made a mistake, but Gaunt's confidence in Mkoll's abilities was such that he decided there was something strange about the ruin that warranted investigation.{{Fn|2b}}

The structure turned out to be an [[Eldar]] edifice housing the remains of a [[Webway Gate]]. A small force of Eldar from [[Craftworld]] [[Dolthe]] were trying to close the gate before the Chaos forces arrived, and created a [[psychic]] illusion that made the Tanith troopers believe that they were on [[Tanith]], defending against the Chaos invasion that destroyed it. Mkoll fought hard, escaping from the entire Chaos army on foot, even as part of his mind tried to convince him that what he was seeing wasn't real. Mkoll's instincts proved crucial to leading Gaunt and [[Inquisitor]] [[Lilith Abfequarn]] back to the ruin, despite the Eldar glamour. After the Gate was closed and the battle was won, Mkoll said farewell to his wife's memory again.{{Fn|2b}}

Mkoll continued to fight superbly in the name of the Emperor after Monthax. In the closing stages of the [[Siege of Vervunhive]], Mkoll was one of thirty Tanith selected personally by Gaunt to take part in [[Operation Heironymo]], the mission to infiltrate [[The Spike]] and assassinate [[Heritor Asphodel]]{{Fn|3}} and he was also in on the mission to rescue [[Saint Sabbat]]'s remains on [[Hagia]] ahead of the planet's destruction.{{Fn|4}} On [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]], Mkoll was picked for [[Operation Larisel]] but his [[Valkyrie]] was blown from the sky, leading everyone to believe he had been killed.{{Fn|5a}} In fact, Mkoll was miraculously thrown clear of the explosion and survived by activating his parachute, landing on a mountainside beneath the layer of toxic cloud known as the Scald.{{Fn|5b}} Mkoll then proceeded to climb the mountain whilst wearing [[rebreather]] gear and use a narrow support girder running alongside a gas pipe to reach the city of [[Ouranberg]], which he infiltrated in the midst of a pitched battle between the Imperial Guard and [[Blood Pact]].{{Fn|5c}} Using his superlative stealth skills, Mkoll made his way into the enemy HQ and attacked [[Sagittar Slaith]], the target of Operation Larisel. While Mkoll's las-fire proved ineffective against Slaith and his [[loxatl]] bodyguards, he revealed that it was just a distraction to keep Slaith in the room long enough for explosives Mkoll had planted to detonate. The blast knocked Mkoll unconscious but killed Slaith, completing the operation.{{Fn|5d}} 

The Tanith's next campaign was on [[Aexe Cardinal]], where Mkoll supervised the induction of the first non-Tanith recruits into the prestigious scout squad.{{Fn|6}} On [[Herodor]] Mkoll out-stealthed and slew [[Skarwael]], a [[Mandrake]] who was one of [[The Nine]], elite Chaos assassins sent to kill Saint Sabbat by [[Magister]] [[Enok Innokenti]].{{Fn|7}} He was then chosen for the EZ-level insertion/assassination mission to [[Gereon]], leaving [[Caober]] in charge of the scout squad whilst he and [[Mkvenner]] were gone. Mkoll played a vital role in the mission and in the period of guerrilla warfare that followed after the Tanith team were stranded on the enemy-occupied planet, helping train the Gereon resistance into an elite insurgency force.{{Fn|8}}{{Fn|9}} Upon the team's return to the regiment, Mkoll tracked a Chaos [[Stalker]] to its lair on [[Ancreon Sextus]], becoming briefly trapped on an Archenemy staging world connected to Ancreon Sextus by sorcerous portals before escaping along with [[Belladon]] scout trooper [[Wes Maggs]], who would become one of Mkoll's best men.{{Fn|9a}} 

Mkoll would face one of his greatest personal tests on [[Jago]], when his commander [[Ibram Gaunt]] was captured by the enemy and presumed dead. In a supreme display of loyalty to Gaunt, Mkoll abandoned his post and joined [[Eszrah ap Niht]] on a suicide mission into the [[Blood Pact]] camp, ultimately discovering Gaunt tortured but alive and bringing him back to the regiment.{{Fn|10a}}

===Later Service===
Mkoll continued to be a senior officer in the Tanith regiment, and despite his personal reserve word of his deeds reached and piqued the interest of [[Sar Af]], a [[White Scars]] [[Space Marine]] who joined the Ghosts along with two other marines for the duration of the mission to [[Salvation's Reach]].{{Fn|11}} On the journey back from the Reach, Mkoll and Sar Af passed the time by hunting each other through the abandoned decks of the ''[[Highness Ser Armaduke]]''. Mkoll was able to get the drop on Sar Af, an extraordinary feat for an unmodified human, and while Sar Af turned the tables by revealing that his fellow marines [[Kater Holofurnace]] and [[Eadwine]] had joined in the hunt, Mkoll then revealed that he had lined the chamber with fake explosives, and had it been a combat situation he could have sacrificed himself to kill three Astartes, an extremely favourable kill/death ratio from the viewpoint of the [[Imperial Guard]].{{Fn|12}}

Later during the return journey, the ''Highness Ser Armaduke'' suffered an unplanned re-entry into realspace and was attacked by [[V'heduak]] raiders. Extremely disoriented by the sudden re-translation, which jumped the entire regiment and ship's crew ten years into the future, Mkoll prowled the ship's corridors while convinced that he was dead, killing V'heduak without fully understanding the situation.{{Fn|13a}} Eventually returning to his senses, he linked up with [[Ornella Zhukova]], who had advanced ahead of her company, and witnessed her solo capabilities first-hand.{{Fn|13b}} Later, after the regiment had arrived at [[Urdesh]], Mkoll asked Zhukova to join the scout squad.{{Fn|13c}}

When the forces of [[Anakwanar Sek]] launched a full-scale assault on Imperial positions in the city of Eltath, Mkoll was at the forefront of the fighting. Scouting a line of abandoned hulks chained together along the shore, Mkoll discovered a large force of [[Sons of Sek]] advancing unopposed and sent Zhukova back to warn [[Elim Rawne|Rawne]], who was commanding the regiment at the time. Fighting alone, he killed several Sons but was eventually overwhelmed and captured, losing his Tanith warknife in the process. His comrades later discovered the knife near a pile of enemy corpses, and for the second time Mkoll was presumed dead by the regiment.{{Fn|13d}} Mkoll's captors took him to [[Magister]] Sek's hidden island base, where captured Guardsmen were either converted or sacrificed. Kept alive because Sek had decreed the Tanith First to be important to his plans, Mkoll took an enemy [[damogaur]] captive and disguised himself as a Son of Sek, forcing his captive to lead him inside Sek's fortress.{{Fn|14a}} There, Mkoll discovered that Kater Holofurnace and [[Brin Milo]] were being held aboard Sek's ship, and freed them both along with an Urdeshi Colonel named [[Mazho]].{{Fn|14b}} Together, the four of them infiltrated a huge meeting at which Sek planned to address his forces, and while Mazho and Holofurnace were killed, Mkoll and Milo succeeded in chasing the injured Sek through a [[Warp]] portal he had conjured to escape, arriving on a remote Urdeshi island. There, Mkoll shoved a bomb down Sek's gaping maw, explosively killing the most dangerous Archenemy leader in the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade]].{{Fn|14c}}

==Character and Abilities==
At the time of the [[Fortis Binary]] campaign, Mkoll was a youthful-looking man in his mid-fifties with a wiry frame and hair that was just starting to turn grey. A woodsman by trade, Mkoll spent his early adulthood in the [[nalwood]] forests of [[Tanith]], and learned to sense and interpret the smallest change in his environment. A born hunter, he carried this skill with him as a scout when he joined the Guard. His ability was so innate that he regarded it as a given, and it took Gaunt to suggest to him that it was the result of spending so much time in Tanith's shifting woods.{{Fn|1i}}

'''Ob'lotai''' is a skilled [[T'au]] [[Battlesuit]] pilot and a member of [[The Eight]], [[Farsight]]'s elite honour guard. The [[Battlesuit]] recently known as '''Ob'lotai 9-0''' is crewed by a a late-generation [[AI|A.I.]] engram of the original Ob'lotai, who taught the young Farsight the basics of piloting a Battlesuit.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}

===History===
Ob'lotai, then known as 4-0, first joined Farsight's service during the [[Arkunasha War]]. He served with Farsight throughout the [[Farsight Expedition]], war on [[Arthas Moloch]], the [[Battle of Vior'los]] (where he succeeded in destroying the flagship of the [[Scar Lords]]){{Fn|5}}, and battle against [[Hive Fleet Gorgon]]. He either fell or was upgraded multiple times over these battles{{Fn|2b}}, eventually becoming Ob'lotai 9-0 during the war against the [[Tyranids]] on [[Vior'los]]. During said war, he helped take down a [[Hive Tyrant]] with his new [[Railgun]] systems.{{Fn|4}}

During the [[Second Agrellan Campaign]] Ob'lotai was badly damaged protecting Farsight from an [[Imperial]] [[Eversor Assassin]], though his actions allowed the rest of The Eight to destroy the creature.{{Fn|6}}

During the final assault on [[Dregrokk]] in the [[War of Dakka]], Ob'lotai 9-0s Battlesuit was badly damaged by Ork fire.{{Fn|3a}} Oblotai 10-0 reappeared in a [[Drone]] afterwards, but the A.I. engram was so damaged in the battle that [[O'Vesa]] was unsure whether he could ever be used to pilot a battlesuit again.{{Fn|3b}}

===Wargear===
Ob'lotai consists of a modified [[XV88 Broadside Battlesuit]] equipped with twin-linked high-yield [[Missile Pod]]s, twin-linked [[Smart Missile System]]s, a [[Seeker Missile]], two [[Missile Drone]]s, and [[Velocity Tracker]].{{Fn|1a}} The suit has also been seen wielding [[Railgun]]s.{{Fn|4}}

===Trivia===
{{Trivia}}
===={{Endn|Notes}}====
*Ob'lotai's name changes with each iteration of the A.I. The earliest Ob'lotai we know of is '''Ob'lotai 4-0'''{{Fn|5}} (though presumedly Ob'lotais 1-0 through 3-0 existed). At the end of [[Farsight: Blade of Truth (Novel)]] Ob'lotais 10-0 through to 20-0 are introduced. It is uncertain if the Ob'lotai 10-0 iteration in '''Blade of Truth''' runs the same engram as Ob'lotai 10-0 in [[Arks of Omen: Farsight]].{{Fn|3b}}

Obax Zakayo.wikitext:
{{IronWarriorsPortal}}
'''Obax Zakayo''' was a [[Chaos Space Marine]] of the [[Iron Warriors]].

==History==
Originally a [[Lieutenant (Space Marine)|Lieutenant]] during the [[Horus Heresy]]{{Fn|3}}, Zakayo mentioned once having fought at the side of [[Warsmith]]s [[Forrix]] and [[Berossus]].{{Fn|1a}} By [[M41]], Zakayo traveled in the entourage of [[Warsmith]] [[Honsou]] on [[Medrengard]], having transferred his allegiance after [[Khalan-Ghol]]'s previous castellan, [[Barban Falk]], ascended to become a [[Daemon Prince]].{{Fn|1a}} Honsou barely tolerated Zakayo's presence, feeling the same disdain for him as he did for most [[Horus Heresy|Heresy]]-era Marines, believing them too bound by the "older" strategies that had dominated the Legion since the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1b}} However, Zakayo was a natural genius with explosives and demolitions, and Honsou badly needed his expertise in the weeks following Honsou's return to Medrengard, when Khalan-Ghol was besieged by Warsmiths [[Toramino]] and Berossus.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}

When the exiled [[Ultramarines]] [[Uriel Ventris]] and [[Pasanius Lysane]] infiltrated Khalan-Ghol, along with [[Colonel]] [[Mikail Leonid]] of the [[Imperial Guard]], [[Ardaric Vaanes]], and the [[Unfleshed]], Zakayo was caught unawares and captured, and crippled by the Unfleshed. Such was his torment that he begged Ventris to kill him, in exchange for information on how to topple the fortress by releasing the [[Heart of Blood]] from its prison inside. Ventris agreed, but Leonid, who had watched the Iron Warriors overrun the [[Imperial]] citadel on [[Hydra Cordatus]] and had suffered horrific torments as their prisoner on Medrengard, refused to execute Zakayo, preferring to let him linger for a few more agonizing hours.{{Fn|1x}}

Zakayo was presumably killed in the collapse of Khalan-Ghol.

Several months later, during the [[Invasion of Ultramar]], Honsou joined a small raiding party traveling through the caves of [[Calth]], seeking the lost tomb of Ultramarines hero [[Remus Ventanus]]. Honsou remarked to [[Cadaras Grendel]] that Zakayo, if he were still alive, would say Honsou was being foolish by putting himself in danger on such an errand. Grendel rejoined that Zakayo would be right, and Honsou agreed with a laugh, saying that it still felt good.{{Fn|2}}

(XIII Legion) **[[Scythes of the Emperor]] |Notes = }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''', the [[Warden of the Pharos]], was the first [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Scythes of the Emperor]] [[Chapter]] and a veteran of the [[Horus Heresy]].{{fn|3}} ===Biography=== Oberdeii was a [[Space Marine Scout|Scout]] of the [[Ultramarines]]' [[199th Company (Ultramarines Legion)|199th 'Aegida' Company]] during the [[Horus Heresy]]. Still in training under [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Arkus]] by the [[Shadow Crusade]], he was stationed on [[Sotha]] where he experienced a prophetic vision of an impending disaster upon his world after venturing inside the [[Pharos (Device)|Pharos]].{{Fn|2}} He was investigated by the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion's]] [[Librarian]]s for any [[Chaos|taint]], but despite his fears of rejection into the Ultramarines he was cleared.{{Fn|1a}} His visions, including the predicted arrival of the [[Blood Angels]] in [[Imperium Secundus]] and the [[Battle of Sotha]], went unheeded.{{Fn|3}} After Arkus died early in the [[Night Lords]] [[Battle of Sotha|attack on Sotha]], Oberdeii led his scout squad to the surface of the planet, where they fought alongside the [[Ultramar Auxilia|Auxilia]] of [[Mericus Giraldus]].{{Fn|1b}} Oberdeii survived the battle, and upon debriefing with [[Roboute Guilliman]] was promoted to a [[Reconnaissance Marine|Reconnaissance Squad]] Sergeant by the [[Primarch]] personally.{{Fn|1c}} Oberdeii was later promoted to [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the Aegida Company, which was maintained by Guilliman's own will even after the [[Second Founding]] as a phantom "11th Company" in defiance of the ''[[Codex Astartes]]''. As [[Warden of the Pharos]], he swore the 'Aegidan Oath' on the ''[[Gladius Incandor]]'' to protect Sotha from whatever secrets had been buried in the Pharos. The oath of moment, written by the primarch's hand, was kept within the Pharos with the skull-mask of [[Barabas Dantioch]], first Warden of the Pharos.{{Fn|3}} By the time of the [[Third Founding]], Oberdeii was the last surviving member of the Aegida Company. Seeking to remove evidence of Guilliman's defiance of his own ''Codex'', Chapter Master [[Tigris Decon]] sent [[Chaplain]] [[Segas]] to Sotha to offer Oberdeii a choice - reassignment to the [[5th Company (Ultramarines)|5th Company]] or continuing to guard the Pharos by becoming Master of a new 'Aegida Chapter'. Oberdeii, initially appalled that [[Rogal Dorn]] had initiated another founding, reluctantly agreed to found a new Chapter, but chose to name them the [[Scythes of the Emperor]].{{Fn|3}} ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} *Oberdeii's proclamation for the people of Sotha to "...turn their ploughshares into swords...", is a reversal of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swords_to_ploughshares concept of "swords to ploughshares"], fitting for [[Warhammer 40,000|a grim darkness in which there is only war]]. ===See also=== *[[List of Chapter Masters]] *[[List of Space Marine Chapter Founders]] ===Sources=== *1: [[Pharos (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: Chapter 2 **{{Endn|1b}}: Chapter 16 **{{Endn|1c}}: Chapter 31 *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Heart of the Pharos (Audio Drama)]] *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Aegidan Oath (Short Story)]] [[Category:Characters (Scythes of the Emperor)]] [[Category:Characters (Ultramarines)]]

'''[[Vargard]] Obyron''' is a powerful [[Necron Lord]] of the [[Sautekh Dynasty]] who serves as the personal bodyguard to [[Necron Overlord|Overlord]] [[Zahndrekh]].{{Fn|1}} 

===Overview===
Unlike his master, Obyron is well aware of the realities of his existence and is fully lucid but has long since abandoned attempts to awaken Zahndrekh to reality.  He attends to all the loose ends of his master's eccentricities and is extremely loyal, willing to give his life for Zahndrekh. Zahndrekh would have died long ago had it not been for Obyron, who has personally put down rebellions by members of [[Gidrim]]'s court attempting to take advantage of the Nemesor's mental state as well as dispatching dangerous prisoners Zahndrekh has deemed honorable.{{Fn|3}} In combat, the duo have proven to be almost undefeatable.{{Fn|1a}}

Obyron's combat prowess was such that in 831.[[M41]] he defeated both [[White Scars]] [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Kor'sarro Khan]], [[Eldar]] [[Ranger]] [[Illic Nightspear]], and many escaped prisoners in simultaneous combat.{{Fn|1b}}

While Obyron is the well-known bodyguard for Zahndrekh, he is a ferocious military commander in his own right.  He also possesses the ability to cut through dimensions and reappear across the battlefield, taking with him any of the units that he commands.  It is a great way to ensure Vargard Obyron's incredible skills are employed against the most worthy enemy.{{Fn|2}}

Octavian (Chapter Ancient).wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''Octavian''' is the [[Chapter Ancient]] of the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter]] and is a hero of the [[Battle for Macragge]],{{Fn|6a}} along with countless other campaigns.{{Fn|6b}}

==Biography==
Before becoming a [[Chapter Ancient]],{{Fn|6a}} Octavian was a [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] in the [[Ultramarines]] [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]], under [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Cato Sicarius]]. His [[Tactical Squad]] was nicknamed the "Swords of Judgment", and they received a collective total of fifteen [[Marksman's Honour]] badges, for their uncanny precision with ranged weaponry.{{Fn|1a}}

===Battle for Macragge===
Octavian had been serving the Ultramarines for decades{{Fn|4}} when the [[Chapter]]'s [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] took part in the [[Battle for Macragge]] during the [[First Tyrannic War]].{{Fn|5}} As the battle-hardened{{Fn|4}} Sergeant led the "Swords of Judgment" in the defence of their [[Adeptus Astartes Homeworld|homeworld]] against the [[Tyranids]] of [[Hive Fleet Behemoth]]{{Fn|5}} the Ultramarines received a distress call from the [[Imperial Navy Lieutenant]] [[Varras]]. The Tyranids had attacked his [[Imperial Lander|Lander]], but Varras had survived a crash landing onto [[Macragge]] and requested help from the [[Chapter]], as he carried one of their [[gene-seed]] canisters. They would need to reach him quickly though, as the Lieutenant was fending off attacks by the [[Xenos]].{{Fn|5a}} Octavian's squadron was charged with rescuing Varras and the gene-seed canister,{{Fn|5b}} but it would be split in half to complete their mission.{{Fn|5c}} One half would be led by the Sergeant and would be dropped off near the Lieutenant,{{Fn|5b}} while the other half would act as reinforcements and would be led by [[Atreus (Chapter Ancient)|Atreus]].{{Fn|5c}} Octavian's squadron soon successfully rescued Varras{{Fn|5d}} and was then reunited with Atreus' squadron. The Lieutenant and the "Swords of Judgment" then fought their way clear of the Tyranids and were evacuated by the '''''Cestus'''''.{{Fn|5e}}

The squadron later aided the [[Ultramarines]] in defending part of a defensive cordon that the [[Chapter]] had established against the [[Hive Fleet Behemoth]]. It was designed to prevent the [[Tyranids]] from gaining further access to [[Macragge]]'s surface, but the [[Xenos]] sent a large force to attack the cordon.{{Fn|5f}} This led Octavian's section to come under increasing pressure and an [[Assault Marine]] squadron, led by [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Furiae]], was sent to aid the beleaguered "Swords of Judgment". The two squads then worked together to combat the Tyranids and they then launched a successful counteroffensive that regained the ground Octavian had lost to Hive Fleet Behemoth.{{Fn|5g}}

===Black Reach===
During the [[Assault on Black Reach]] in '''855.[[M41]]'''{{Fn|1b}}, the "Swords of Judgment" were deployed to [[Black Reach]] with the rest of the Second Company against [[Waaagh! Zanzag]].  During the liberation of [[Ghospora Hive]] from the [[Ork]]s, the Squad took severe casualties; after their precise [[Boltgun|bolter]] fire had downed an Ork flyer, one of their [[Brother]]s, [[Castor (Ultramarines)|Castor]], threw himself onto a dropped bomb to protect others from the blast.  Despite this heroic act, several of his squad were killed or severely wounded.{{Fn|2a}} The remnants of the Swords were rallied for the final push against the Orks, and accompanied Sicarius and the rest of the company to hunt down the Orks' [[Warboss]], [[Zanzag]].{{Fn|2b}}

===Espandor===
During the attack of the [[Bloodborn]] on [[Ultramar]], in '''854.999.M41'''{{Fn|1b}}, the 2nd Company was deployed to [[Espandor]].{{Fn|3}}

===Ichar IV Campaign===
During the [[Second Tyrannic War]]'s [[Ichar IV Campaign]], Octavian was the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Chapter Champion]], while [[Atreus (Chapter Ancient)|Atreus]] was its [[Chapter Ancient]].{{Fn|6a}}

===13th Black Crusade===
He was later part{{Fn|6a}} of the [[Ultramarines Honour Guard]] [[Space Marine Company|Company]] that their [[Chapter]] sent to aid the [[Cadian Subsector]] during the [[13th Black Crusade]].{{Fn|6}} By then, Octavian had become the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Chapter Ancient]], after the previous incumbent, [[Atreus (Chapter Ancient)|Atreus]], was killed in battle. Sometime during the war, the [[Imperium]] learned that [[Abaddon the Despoiler]]'s [[Blackstone Fortress]], ''[[Will of Eternity]]'', was going to attack [[Cadia]]. Its first target, though, was [[Kasr Partox]], where Cadia's [[Lord Castellan]] [[Ursarkar E. Creed]] was located. Efforts had been made to send [[vox]] messages to the Lord Castellan so that he could evacuate from the Kasr, but Partox's comms were down and so he would need to be warned in person. Octavian was chosen to deliver the message and would take with him an Honour Guard squadron, along with the Ultramarines' [[Chapter Champion]].{{Fn|6a}} 

They then deployed to [[Kasr Partox]], from the [[Battle Barge]] ''[[Aeternus]]'',{{Fn|6a}} and fought their way through the [[Chaos]] forces that had invaded it. As the [[Ultramarines Honour Guard|Honour Guard]] squadron neared the [[Lord Castellan]]'s position, though, they were suddenly attacked by a [[Chaos Undivided]] [[Daemon Prince]], who wielded the [[Darkblade]].{{Fn|6c}} Despite their skills and bravery, the Prince was able to kill many of the Honour Guard squadron's members with the [[Daemon Weapon]], before they were finally able to banish it back to the [[Warp]].{{Fn|6d}} With the Prince defeated, Octavian, the [[Chapter Champion]] and the three remaining Honor Guards, were able to deliver their warning to [[Ursarkar E. Creed]]. The Lord Castellan thanked them for doing so and then began making preparations to evacuate his forces to [[Kasr Gallan]], before the ''Will of Eternity'' destroyed Kasr Partox. With their mission complete, a [[Thunderhawk]] was sent to evacuate Octavian and his surviving forces.{{Fn|6e}}

Odoski.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Commissar]] who was part of the [[Imperium|Imperium's]] forces defending [[Cadia]] during the [[13th Black Crusade]].{{Fn|1}}

While fighting against the [[Chaos]] invasion, Commissar {{PAGENAME}} and the '''Cadia 309th Armoured''' and '''''The Sureshots'' 822nd Infantry''' [[Imperial Guard Regiment|Regiments]], were coming to the aid of the Imperium forces fighting in the '''Dhorak front''', when they were ambushed by the [[Alpha Legion]].  As the ambush unfolded around them, the Commissar took command and began giving orders to the two Regiments, but knew instantly he needed to extract himself from the immediate battle in order to set up a proper firing line that would punish the attacking Chaos forces.  Unfortunately, this played right into the Alpha Legion's hands and as Commissar {{PAGENAME}} began a fighting retreat, the Alpha Legion summoned [[Daemon]]s amidst the Regiments' rear ranks.  In the massacre that followed the Commissar and every member of the two Regiments were killed and the dwindling Imperium forces fighting in the Dhorak front never received the reinforcements they had been depending on.{{Fn|1}}

Oenomaus.wikitext:
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Human]] Gladiator-slave that lived upon [[Nuceria]] during the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}}

Living in the same cave-prison as the young [[Angron]] in the city of Desh'ea, the older {{PAGENAME}} became his mentor and the closest thing he had to a father. The two formed a deep bond and reaped many victories in the gladiatorial arenas of Nuceria, which culminated in the two defeating two Berserk [[Ogryn]]s equipped with the [[Butcher's Nails]]. After this victory, the masters of Desh'ea, known as the ''High Riders'', demanded that the two battle one another to the death. However Angron refused and openly insulted the High Riders, which resulted in Angron being implemented with the Butcher's Nails as a form of punishment.{{Fn|1a}} Upon being imbued with the Nails, Angron was loosed upon {{PAGENAME}} and tore him apart in a blind frenzy. Upon regaining his senses Angron realized what he had done and was driven to such despair that he unleashed a bestial howl that lasted for days.{{Fn|1b}}

==Trivia==

[[wikipedia:Oenomaus (rebel slave)|Oenomaus]] was the name of a Roman gladiator and later general in Spartacus' slave army.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Rune Priest]] of the [[Space Wolves]]' [[Great Company|5th Company]], during the [[Great Crusade]] and the early stages of the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}} 

===Biography===
Accompanying [[Wolf Lord]] [[Amlodhi Skarssen Skarssensson]] on a mission to demand the [[Thousand Sons]] assist the VI in the [[Ark Reach Cluster]], he first met [[Ahzek Ahriman]] when he saved the [[Chief Librarian]] from [[Warp]] predators on [[Aghoru]].{{Fn|1b}} They struck up a friendship{{fn|1c}} and fought side by side{{fn|1d}} against the [[Chaos|corruption]] that had lain dormant under the planet's artificial Mountain{{fn|1e}}, complementing each other's battle style{{fn|1f}}.

On the way to the Ark Reach Cluster, the two learnt from each other's different perspectives and practices of [[Psyker|psykana]]{{fn|1g}}, but during the last battle of the Compliance Wyrdmake bore witness to one of the Thousand Sons succumbing to the [[Thousand_Sons#Geneseed|flesh change]]{{fn|1h}}. This event, and the knowledge the Rune Priest had gathered from Ahriman, led him to speak against the XV at the [[Council of Nikaea]], denouncing Magnus and his gene-sons as sorcerers.{{fn|1i}}

Wyrdmake was present at the [[Burning of Prospero]], overseeing the destruction of the [[Great Library of Tizca]] and extracting Ahriman's location from a dying [[Ankhu Anen]].{{fn|1j}} He was forced into a psychic duel by the Chief Librarian, who broke his spirit by showing him the [[Horus Heresy|Age of Darkness]] born of the battle, and had his soul obliterated by voracious warp predators.{{fn|1k}}

{{CrimsonSlaughterPortal}}
'''Okrark''' is current Chief [[Dark Apostle]] of the [[Crimson Slaughter]].

==Biography==
In 928.[[M41]]{{Fn|1a}}, Okrark was the [[Master of Sanctity|Master of the Reclusiam]] of the [[Crimson Sabres]]. When the Crimson Sabres began burning the bodies of the people of [[Umidia]], Okrark assured the [[Scout]]s of the Tenth Company that they were giving proper burial to the loyal citizens of Umidia who had been killed by [[Chaos Cult]]ists. When several [[Scout Sergeant]]s pointed out that many of the slain had injuries caused by [[boltgun]]s, Okrark told the Sergeants that they had been collaborators who had been executed for heresy.{{Fn|2}}

When the Crimson Sabres journeyed into the [[Eye of Terror]], Okrark initially remained steadfast in his devotions to the [[Emperor of Mankind]]. However, as time went on, and the Crimson Sabres became more mutated, Okrark's sermons began to focus less on the righteousness of the [[Imperium]] of [[Human|Man]] and brotherhood, and more about the acquisition of power for its own sake and the strength of the Crimson Sabres.{{Fn|1b}} When [[Chapter Master]] [[Sevastus Kranon]] expressed a desire to end the curse and make a new life, Okrark was one of those he gathered and who agreed with his plans.{{Fn|1c}}

'''Ollanius "Olly" Piers''' was a [[Corporal]] in the [[Hundred and Fifth Tercio Upland Grenadiers]] [[Imperial Army]] [[Regiment]], during the [[Battle for Terra]]. His fate would become heavily tied to the legend of [[Ollanius Pius]].{{Fn|1a}}

===History===
He was named after his grandfather, but he disliked his first name so much that he went by Olly instead. Piers was known to be a boisterous person, who liked to tell stories about himself that were usually lies or extremely exaggerated{{Fn|1a}}. He was also secretly a worshiper of the warrior-goddess [[Mythrus]] and believed in the divinity of the [[Emperor]]. Though due such beliefs being against the [[Imperial Truth]] he made sure to be careful who he shared this with. As the forces of the traitorous [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] attacked the [[Imperial Palace]], Piers was among the Imperial Army forces sent by convoy to defend the [[Eternity Wall Spaceport]]. During the journey he struck up a friendship with the historian [[Hari Harr]], who was among the small number of [[Remembrancer]]s that [[Kyril Sindermann]] had created at the [[Primarch]] [[Dorn]]'s request. As Hari looked through his [[dataslate]], Piers discovered that he had a copy of the [[Lectitio Divinitatus]] on it, which led him to speak about his religious beliefs to the historian.{{Fn|1b}} 

As they neared the space port, however, they came under attack by Horus' forces and the convoy was destroyed. Piers, escaped from the wreckage with Hari and a few other survivors, but they were soon pursued by [[Daemon]] [[possessed]] humans. As the most senior rank amongst the survivors and knowing they could not reach the space port in time, Piers prepared the group to defend themselves. When the possessed neared them, they opened fire at Piers' command, but while they were able to kill many of the Daemons, the possessed soon closed in on the survivors. The Daemons' began killing them and any organized defense broke down, as the survivors fought to defend themselves. Piers heroically defended Hari and managed to single handily kill a few of the Daemons before he ran out of ammo. As they faced their deaths, Piers apologized to Hari, as the Daemons closed in on them, but it was at that moment their deliverance arrived. The [[Sisters of Silence]] [[Knight-Commander]] [[Jenetia Krole]] had also been making her way to the space port and intervened to save the survivors. Her [[Blank]] powers, caused the Daemons to retreat, but because of her abilities they made her invisible to most people. While Hari and the other survivors had seen the Daemons retreated for no reason, Piers could see Krole and mistakenly believed she was the goddess [[Mythrus]], who had heard his prayers. He then prostrated himself before Krole and thanked her for saving them, though, to the Hari and the others it looked like he was talking to no one but air.{{Fn|1c}} 

Afterwards, Piers and the others reached the space port, where he began spreading his exploits to anyone who listed. He was later among the [[Imperial]] forces that defended the [[Pons Solar]] bridge, that connected the space port to the Eternity Wall. Hari was beside him, despite Piers constant attempts to get him to leave, as the front-lines were no place for civilians. Hari refused, though, as it was his job to record what happened during Terra's invasion. Soon afterwards, however, the [[Warmaster]]'s forces attacked in strength and swept away the defenders. As their comrades fell around them, Piers grabbed Hari and began leading him away to safety, though, they both knew he wanted to escape as well. They then came across two soldiers struggling to lift up a banner of the [[Emperor]], after their three comrades who had aided them, had been killed. Hari was suddenly struck with a desire to help in anyway he could, even if it was insignificant, and rushed to help lift up the banner. Piers quickly joined him and other surviving soldiers saw the banner aloft and rallied to their side as well, as the bridge's defenses fell apart. Soon a large number of soldiers were at their side and they began praying to the Emperor as they held his banner. Just then, however, a [[World Eater]] approached them, and fear threatened to overwhelm them as they fired upon the Traitor. Their firepower could not stop the [[Chaos Space Marine]], but just before he reached Piers and the others, Knight-Commander [[Jenetia Krole]] intervened once more and killed the World Eater with a single blow. Like before, however, only Piers could see her and for the others it appeared that the Emperor had answered their prayers and struck down the Traitor.{{Fn|1a}}

As they gave thanks to the Emperor, Krole got Piers' attention and signaled that they should retreat. He then rallied the others and claimed the Emperor and [[Mythrus]] had saved them as he led them away further into the space port{{Fn|1d}}. Afterwards the Imperium's forces began to prepare for the Traitors' next attack, after the Pons Solar bridge fell to them, and Piers started to repair the damage done to the banner the soldiers had carried. It was at that time, Hari arrived and told Piers he wanted to record the soldier's life as part of the histories he was collecting, during the battle. At first Piers refused, but relented as long as Hari used the name Olympos, as he felt it was a more heroic name than Ollanius. Hari refused, but then Piers asked that he at least made his story appear grander than life. Instead of saying he helped carry a banner bearing the image of the Emperor, Hari was encouraged to write that Piers defended the Emperor himself from the [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]], during the battle. Hari once more refused, as he felt no one would ever believe it.{{Fn|1a}}

Later during the fall of the Eternity Wall Spaceport, Piers defended a banner with the image of the Emperor emblazoned on it. He even stood his ground as [[Angron]] himself appeared. Piers refused to flee, instead firing his weapon as the Red Angel charged him, shouting "Throne of Terra!" as he was slain.{{Fn|1e}}

Oltyx.wikitext:
{{Character |Portal ={{NecronsPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =Oltyx.jpg |Caption =Lord Oltyx{{Fn|1g}} |Title =The Twice-Dead King
[[Valgûl]]{{Fn|2e}} |Homeworld ='' '' *[[Sedh]] (Former) *[[Antikef]] (Former) *[[Drazak]]{{Fn|2e}} |Birth =c. 65 million B.C. |Active Period =??? - Present |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species ='' '' *[[Necrontyr]] (Former) *[[Necron]] |Type =[[Flayed One]]{{Fn|2e}} |Gender =Male |Relatives ='' '' *[[Unnas]] (Father) *[[Djoseras]] (Brother) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Necron Lord]] of [[Sedh]] (Former) *[[Phaeron]] of the [[Ithakas Dynasty]] (Former) *[[Flayer King]] of [[Drazak]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Necrons]] **[[Infinite Empire]] (Former) **[[Ithakas Dynasty]] (Former) **[[Drazak|The Bone Kingdom]] |Notes = }} '''Oltyx''', the '''Twice-Dead King''', was a [[Necron Lord]] and later [[Phaeron]], originally of the [[Ithakas Dynasty]].{{Fn|1a}} ===History=== Born to [[Phaeron]] [[Unnas]] and constantly overshadowed by his elder brother [[Djoseras]], the [[Necrontyr]] Oltyx was originally a veteran of the [[Second War of Succession]] against the [[Ogdobekh Dynasty]]. Fortunately for Oltyx, [[biotransference]] into [[Necron]] bodies began just as he was breaking out in the cancerous tumors that were typical of his race. Reborn in a mechanical body, he fought in the [[War in Heaven (Necron)|War in Heaven]] and took part in the [[Great Sleep]]. However the Ithakas Dynasty had reawoken earlier to most others, and Oltyx used the opportunity to try and usurp both his father and brother. The plot was foiled by [[Djoseras]], who promptly exiled the fallen lord for the attempted regicide. Unknown to Oltyx, the act served to save his life.{{Fn|1a}} Years later, Oltyx was still in exile overseeing the crumbling Ithakas backwater of [[Sedh]]. The monotony of his existence soon changed however when a large [[Ork]] force arrived, and Oltyx personally slew the [[Warboss]] overseeing the invasion.{{Fn|1b}} It soon became apparent that the Greenskins had been fleeing from an enormous [[Imperial]] [[Crusade]], and in order to survive Oltyx and his followers had to flee Sedh. They made for [[Antikef]], the [[Tomb World|Crownworld]] of the Ithakas Dynasty, in order to seek aid against the Crusade.{{Fn|1b}} When Oltyx arrived on Antikef, he found the Dynasty in madness and ruin. His father Unnas had succumb to the [[Flayer Curse]] and was being manipulated by the corrupt Vizier [[Hemiun]]. Seeking to restore sanity to his Dynasty, Oltyx attempted to usurp Unnas but was captured and tortured by Hemiun, who forced him to battle in gladiatorial arenas against [[Flayed Ones]] and captive [[Xenos]].{{Fn|1c}} Oltyx escaped with the help of his [[Cryptek]] [[Mentep]], but was ultimately saved thanks to the return of his brother [[Djoseras]], who took his rightful place as the Dynasty's heir. Shortly after [[Djoseras]]'s arrival came the Imperial Crusade, which began the process of laying waste to Antikef.{{Fn|1d}} Together, [[Djoseras]] and Oltyx organized the defense of Antikef as the Ithakas Dynasty began to evacuate the world. In the face of [[Angels Encarmine]] [[Space Marine]]s and [[Imperial Titan]]s, the ruined and vastly outnumbered Dynasty stood little hope of survival otherwise. In the final stages of the battle [[Djoseras]] volunteered himself to stay behind and was slain fighting Space Marines as the Ithakas fleet fled. Oltyx encountered the now completely feral Unnas and finally put his father out of his misery. Oltyx became the new master of the Ithakas Dynasty at last, but ironically he felt no satisfaction.{{Fn|1e}} The Imperial Crusade continued to chase the now-refugee Ithakas fleet under Oltyx's command. Under Mentep's guidance, the group first fled to a weapon known as the [[Gravitic Trebuchet]], but even this device proved unable to stop the endless Imperial tide.{{Fn|2a}} Now even more desperate, they arrived at the blighted realm of the insane Cryptek [[Am-Heht]] who had once been Mentep's former master. During the subsequent meeting with Am-Heht, Mentep was restored with his memory of the [[Ghostwind]], which the Cryptek insisted was the key to the Dynasty's survival.{{Fn|2b}} Afterwards, Oltyx learned from Mentep and his Admiral [[Yenekh]] that vast numbers of Flayed Ones had been stored within the bowels of their fleet without his approval. Worse still, Mentep revealed that the intelligence of Oltyx's flagship ''Akrops'' was using the Ghostwind to journey to the mythical but cursed world of [[Drazak]]. The revelation drove Oltyx into a rage and he slew Mentep while banishing Yenekh, who himself was near to fully succumbing to the Flayer Curse. Oltyx then oversaw a vicious purge of the Flayed Ones within his fleet.{{Fn|2c}} In the midst of the chaotic purge, [[Angels Encarmine]] and their allies came upon the Ithakas refugee fleet once more.{{Fn|2d}} In the subsequent fighting against [[Terminator]]s and a [[Dreadnought]] aboard the bridge of his flagship Oltyx died for the second time, just as he had succeeded in activating the Ghostwind protocol out of desperation.{{Fn|2d}} Oltyx miraculously rose once more days later amidst the ruins of his fleet, now orbiting Drazak. Discovering he too had since succumbed to the Flayer Curse, Oltyx embraced his destiny and led the survivors of Ithakas to Drazak. On the world he took up the mantle of [[Valgûl]], the Fallen Lord.{{Fn|2e}} It is unclear if Oltyx was always destined to become the mythical Flayer King and had traveled back in time via the Ghostwind, or he simply was a new bearer of the title. ===Subordinate Minds=== Thanks to his [[Cryptek]] [[Mentep]], Oltyx was able to divide his consciousness into a number of specialist sub-minds that each performed a task. These sub-minds were capable of conversing with Oltyx as well as each other and even kept secrets from him. Oltyx was stripped of these minds while captive on Antikef, but they later lived on in the form of a [[Scarab]].{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1d}} Oltyx's five subordinate minds were:{{Fn|1f}} *'''Doctrinal''': Derived from Oltyx's understanding of Necron/Necrontyr culture, history, and traditions. *'''Strategic''': Derived from Oltyx's understanding of military strategy. *'''Combat''': Derived from Oltyx's understanding of martial prowess and close-combat. *'''Analytical''': Derived from Oltyx's understanding of processing and analyzing information and data. *'''Xenology''': Derived from Oltyx's understanding of other alien species. ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[The Twice-Dead King: Ruin (Novel)]] **{{Endn|1a}}: Chapters 1-3 **{{Endn|1b}}: Chapters 4-5 **{{Endn|1c}}: Chapters 9-11 **{{Endn|1d}}: Chapters 14-17 **{{Endn|1e}}: Chapters 19-21 **{{Endn|1f}}: Dramatis Necronae **{{Endn|1g}}: Cover *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Twice-Dead King: Reign (Novel)]] **{{Endn|2a}}: Chapters 7-8 **{{Endn|2b}}: Chapters 11-12 **{{Endn|2c}}: Chapters 13-15 **{{Endn|2d}}: Chapters 17-19 **{{Endn|2e}}: Chapters 20-Epilogue [[Category:Characters (Necrons)]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}, the Warmaker,''' was a member of the [[Thousand Sons]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]], where he was severely wounded while fighting the [[Eldar]]. His injuries required him to be interred within a [[Space Marine Dreadnought|Dreadnought]], but he would fight again - not just in the Great Crusade and the [[Horus Heresy]] that followed, but also in the [[Long War]] the Thousand Sons have waged against the [[False Emperor]] for ten thousand years.{{Fn|1}}

The Long War however, has been hard on the mind and sanity of the Warmaker, as the corrupted auto-senses of his Dreadnought's armour, which has long since been [[Chaos|corrupted]] into that of a [[Helbrute]], only show him the battles and enemies of his past. This has caused him to believe that he is still fighting ten thousand years ago and anyone who faces the Warmaker must contend with the seething hatred this causes him to unleash in battle. Adding to his misfortune is that Onoris has always heeded the words of the [[Sorcerer]] [[Ahriman]], ever since the time of their Legion, and the Sorcerer now puts the Warmaker's constant rage to good use against his numerous enemies. The latest foes Ahriman has unleashed Onoris upon are the [[Harlequin]]s of the [[Masque of the Twisted Path]], who are attempting to stop the Sorcerer's most current attempt to reach the [[Black Library]].{{Fn|1}}

Ordamael.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
'''Ordamael''' was a [[Blood Angels]] [[Chaplain]], who served as his [[Chapter]]'s [[Paternis Sanguis]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
It is the second highest [[Paternis Sanguis|rank]] in the [[Blood Angels]]' [[Reclusiam]] and as such, Ordamael often acted in the stead of the ever-absent [[High Chaplain]] [[Astorath]]{{Fn|1a}}. Such was the case for the [[Cryptus Campaign]]{{Fn|2}} and when [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]] [[Devastation of Baal|invaded]] [[Baal]], as Astorath was taking part in the [[Diamor Campaign]]{{Fn|1a}}. In the battle against the Hive Fleet, Ordamael defended the Chapter's [[Fortress Monastery]] and weeks later found himself to be among the last of the [[Imperial]] forces still fighting to protect Baal. With their doom at hand, [[Chapter Master|Commander]] [[Dante]] ordered the surviving members of the [[Sanguinary Brotherhood]] to launch a final charge into Leviathan's invading forces and Ordamael fought beside Dante as they struck the [[Tyranids]]. However the Paternis Sanguis soon met his end, when Ordamael was torn in half by a giant Tyranid beast.{{Fn|1b}}
